d: In 1991, India was forced to pledge its gold reserves overseas to secure emergency loans as a balance of payments crisis pushed the country to the brink. Thirty-five years later, the direction has reversed. The Reserve Bank of India is bringing its gold back home, with domestic holdings now accounting for 84% of the country’s total reserves. In this video, Firstpost examines why the RBI is shifting bullion from foreign vaults to India, how the freezing of Russian central bank assets in 2022 changed the way countries view reserve security, and why other central banks are also repatriating…
